title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals are using generative AI to impersonate real people and create deepfake audio and video for fraud. They clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photographs, and research personal details to build convincing schemes targeting immigrants and others. One immigration attorney had his voice cloned to solicit clients, and individuals lost substantial sums to fake investment and emergency call schemes.

The failure occurred at the point of victim contact, where the impersonation had no verification step. A person receiving a call heard what sounded like a known professional or family member and acted on that alone. The system that failed was trust in audio and video evidence without independent confirmation. What would have caught this was a practice of verifying urgent requests through known contact information and establishing family code words before emergencies occur.

It is not established whether the AI tools used were created for fraud or repurposed from legitimate products, or what the costs and barriers to conducting these scams actually are.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to conduct scams across Georgia and South Florida by creating fake voices, photos, and phone calls that appear legitimate. In one case, a South Florida immigration attorney discovered criminals had cloned his voice to target immigrants, while a Cobb County couple lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in losses from AI-enabled scams last year. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints totaling nearly $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia recorded 71 complaints with over $10.4 million in reported losses.

Scammers use generative AI technology to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photographs, and research personal relationships to make their schemes more convincing. The technology is making traditional scams like romance schemes, investment fraud, and emergency calls harder to recognize. To protect themselves, authorities recommend families establish code words to verify identity during emergencies, verify urgent requests through known phone numbers, and avoid sending money based solely on phone calls. As AI tools become cheaper and more accessible, experts predict these scams will continue evolving, making verification a critical defense against fraud.
